thread.title: Close Update: China Trade Data Triggers Global Growth Worries

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: China Trade Data Triggers Global Growth Worries

organizations.name: china trade data triggers global growth worries shutterstock

text:
Shutterstock photo Stocks closed lower for a second day in a row when global growth concerns resurfaced on bearish Chinese trade data. Led by losses in component stocks Apple ( AAPL ) and Walgreens ( WBA ), the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down as much as 230 points at the open before clawing back losses throughout the day to close just 89 points below Friday's close.
An unexpected plunge in Chinese imports and exports sent shockwaves through global equity markets as waning consumer spending translated into a 7.6% drop in imports and the largest Chinese trade surplus on record.
US equities were trading lower in sympathy with losses in Asia and Europe with the defensive tone exacerbated by lackluster results from Citigroup ( C ), the first of the major banks to report Q4 results.
And although early pressure was mitigated by upbeat comments from President Donald Trump regarding US/China trade talks, the Dow was again unable to break away from the 50% retracement of December's range and orbited this level for a fourth straight day.
The risk-off trade failed to translate into demand for safe havens with the 10-year note cheapening to a 2.702% yield and gold higher by just $2.50. China's trade data weighed on industrial metals as copper dropped to its lowest level in six days. Oil was also lower with Brent crude lower for a third day and West Texas intermediate drifting back to $50/barrel.
In corporate news, Pacific Gas & Electric PCG) became unhinged after the utility disclosed it will file for bankruptcy protection as a result of its liability from the California wildfires, dropping to its lowest level since 2002.
